sample_size.excerpt: Mailed questionnaires were completed by 1279 (691 male and 588 female) newly diagnosed histologically confirmed RCC cases and 5370 (2696 male and 2674 female) population controls between 1994 and 1997 in eight Canadian provinces. cases.excerpt: A total of 1097 incident, histologically confirmed RCC cases and 1476 controls were included in this study. Suitable quantity and quality of genomic DNA was obtained from a subset of 777 (70.8%) eligible RCC cases and 1035 (70.1%) controls enrolled in our study.

comparison.excerpt: Frequency of dietary intake variables categorized into tertiles based on intake among genotyped controls.

timing.excerpt: The questionnaire was repeated for two different time periods: (1) the year prior to interview, and (2) the year prior to political and market changes in 1989 (1991 in Russia).

continent.excerpt: cases and controls from Central and Eastern Europe

exposure_measurement.excerpt: All dietary intake frequencies in this study were assessed in tertiles based on the frequency of dietary intake among controls.

smoking_status.excerpt: All regression models were adjusted for age, sex, study center, smoking status (ever, never), BMI, and self-reported hypertensive status.

studies.Study: Southard EB et al. (2012) [PMID: 22086884] — estimate 1 · Male
studies.Reference: Lead, calcium uptake, and related genetic variants in association with renal cell carcinoma risk in a cohort of male Finnish smokers.
studies.Title: Lead, calcium uptake, and related genetic variants in association with renal cell carcinoma risk in a cohort of male Finnish smokers.
studies.Authors: Southard EB, Roff A, Fortugno T, Richie JP, Kaag M, Chinchilli VM, Virtamo J, Albanes D, Weinstein S, Wilson RT
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.Population: Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene (ATBC) Cancer Prevention Study participants

sample_size.excerpt: Our study utilized a nested case-control study of the ATBC cohort including 154 RCC cases and 308 controls.
sample_size.location: Materials and Methods, paragraph 3; total_n derived from reported group counts 154 + 308 = 462

cases.excerpt: Among 154 newly diagnosed cases and 308 matched controls, RCC was associated with higher whole blood lead (OR=2.0, 95% CI:1.0,3.9; quartile 4 (Q4) v.

effect_size.excerpt: Results for whole blood lead were similar but the magnitude of association was more pronounced using only controls from the VDPP (Q4 v. Q1: OR=3.1, 95% CI: 1.1, 8.4), although the trend was not statistically significant (p-trend=0.300).

p_value.excerpt: Higher total serum calcium (P trend =<0.001) was associated with reduced RCC risk.

design.excerpt: In this nested case-control study, whole blood lead (Pb), total serum calcium, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D were measured in blood drawn prior to diagnosis among male smokers participating in the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study.

timing.excerpt: whole blood lead (Pb), total serum calcium, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D were measured in blood drawn prior to diagnosis

continent.excerpt: ATBC enrolled nearly 30,000 male smokers aged 50–69 years in southwestern Finland from 1985–1988.

ethnicity.excerpt: The Finnish population is generally homogenous

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Total serum calcium was measured by colorimetric assay (BioVision, Mountain View, CA) at the Penn State University Core Endocrine Lab.
exposure_measurement.location: Materials and Methods, Whole Blood Lead, Serum Calcium, and Serum Vitamin D Measurements, paragraph 2

studies.Reference: Nutrition and other risk factors for renal cell carcinoma in postmenopausal women.
studies.Title: Nutrition and other risk factors for renal cell carcinoma in postmenopausal women.
studies.Authors: Prineas RJ, Folsom AR, Zhang ZM, Sellers TA, Potter J
studies.Population: Postmenopausal, predominantly white women in Iowa age 55-69 years and free of cancer
studies.comparison_type: Higher versus lower total dietary calcium intake

sample_size.excerpt: Among 35,192 postmenopausal, predominantly white women in Iowa age 55-69 years and free of cancer, we collected baseline history, dietary information, and anthropometric data by mail in 1986. We ascertained the 8-year incidence (62 new cases) of renal cell carcinoma using the Iowa Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) register, the National Death Index, and mail follow-up.
